item.title: Israeli forces detain 20 Palestinians during searches in besieged Hebron
item.description:
Israeli forces detain 20 Palestinians during searches in besieged Hebron

At least 20 Palestinians have been detained by Israeli forces during the ongoing military siege of Hebron in the occupied West Bank, which has also led to the displacement of more than 2,200 people.

The Palestinian news agency Wafa reported that Israeli forces stormed most neighborhoods of Hebron city, raided and searched homes, and subjected citizens to abuse before detaining several Palestinians.

The forces also raided the towns of Dura, Yatta and as-Samu, south of Hebron, detaining 11 Palestinians after storming their homes and mistreating them. Two more Palestinians were detained in Tarqumiya, west of Hebron, along with others from the town of Halhul to the north.

item.title: Tehran strikes Iranian Kurdish base in Iraq with drones, report says
item.description:
Tehran strikes Iranian Kurdish base in Iraq with drones, report says

Iran's armed forces attacked bases belonging to an Iranian Kurdish opposition group in Iraq's Kurdistan region using drones, Mehr news agency reported.

"As part of a drone operation carried out by the Revolutionary Guards' ground forces, the headquarters of the terrorist and separatist group Komala, located in the Balisan region, was targeted last night," Mehr reported.

Earlier, Reuters reported that an explosive-laden drone attacked an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp northeast of Iraq's Erbil on Saturday night.

The semi-autonomous region hosts camps and bases belonging to several groups of Iranian Kurdish militants, which Iran has targeted repeatedly since the start of the Middle East war in February.

Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant
item.description:
Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant

Russia’s embassy in Tehran has denied reports that Russian embassy staff and specialists working at the Bushehr nuclear power plant are preparing to leave Iran.

“Neither embassy staff nor Russian specialists at the Bushehr nuclear power plant have any plans to evacuate. Work continues as normal,” the embassy said in a statement, dismissing reports to the contrary as “FAKES”.

Bushehr, Iran’s only operating nuclear power plant, has come under repeated attack during the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. Satellite imagery released in July showed damage inside the complex.

item.title: Gwadar in the Regional Energy Equation: Strategic Opportunity or Costly Promise for Pakistan?
item.description: Marine bunkering services have begun at Gwadar. Meanwhile, according to reporting in June 2026, the proposed $10 billion Saudi refinery announced for the port in 2019 had yet to attract the promised investment. These contrasting experiences raise a fundamental question: where should Pakistan begin with Gwadar’s development? The strongest starting point is commercial activity with existing customers and measurable revenue. That can provide a foundation for larger investments. Pakistani fuel, a new market According to a July 2026 announcement by Pakistan’s Port Community System, Gwadar’s inaugural commercial bunkering operation delivered 2,500 tonnes of very low sulphur fuel oil produced by Cnergyico. item.title: Amnesty Indonesia is right, the Foreign Ministry is wrong: Quit Trump’s Board of Peace
item.description: On Thursday, Indonesia’s Foreign Ministry defended the country’s seat on the Board of Peace.
